requirements.quote:
All these messages, except for interim responses and requests
   contained in PUSH_PROMISE (Section 6.6) frames, can optionally
   include a field block that carries a trailer section.
requirements.condition: For requests, final responses, promised requests, and pushed responses other than interim responses and requests contained in PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.required_behavior: The message may include a field block carrying a trailer section.
requirements.why_checkable: Message parsing or generation can verify that trailer field blocks are accepted or emitted only for the identified message categories.

requirements.quote:
lines in a field block carries a single value.  The serialized field
   block is then divided into one or more octet sequences, called field
   block fragments.  The first field block fragment is transmitted
   within the frame payload of HEADERS (Section 6.2) or PUSH_PROMISE
   (Section 6.6), each of which could be followed by CONTINUATION
   (Section 6.10) frames to carry subsequent field block fragments.
requirements.condition: When serializing and transmitting a field block.
requirements.required_behavior: Divide the serialized field block into at least one field block fragment; carry the first fragment in a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame and any subsequent fragments in CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not create a field block with zero fragments or carry its first fragment in a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame traces expose the number, type, and ordering of frames carrying every field block fragment.

requirements.quote:
A receiving endpoint reassembles the field block by concatenating its
   fragments and then decompresses the block to reconstruct the field
   section.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a fragmented field block.
requirements.required_behavior: Concatenate the fragments in order and then decompress the resulting field block to reconstruct the field section.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not decompress fragments independently or reorder them during reassembly.
requirements.why_checkable: A receiver can be tested with multi-fragment blocks whose correct decoding depends on ordered concatenation before decompression.

requirements.quote:
*  a single HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame, with the END_HEADERS flag
      set, or
requirements.condition: When a complete field section is carried in one frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a single HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame with END_HEADERS set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not represent a complete single-frame field section with END_HEADERS unset.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type, frame count, and END_HEADERS flag are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
*  a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame with the END_HEADERS flag unset
      and one or more CONTINUATION frames, where the last CONTINUATION
      frame has the END_HEADERS flag set.
requirements.condition: When a complete field section spans multiple frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Start with a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame whose END_HEADERS flag is unset, follow it with one or more CONTINUATION frames, and set END_HEADERS on the last CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use zero CONTINUATION frames for this form or leave END_HEADERS unset on the last CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame sequence can be checked for its initial type, continuation count, and terminal flag.

requirements.quote:
Each field block is processed as a discrete unit.  Field blocks MUST
   be transmitted as a contiguous sequence of frames, with no
   interleaved frames of any other type or from any other stream.
requirements.condition: While transmitting the frames of a field block.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit all frames of the field block contiguously as one discrete unit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interleave a frame of another type or another stream within the field-block frame sequence.
requirements.why_checkable: A captured frame sequence can detect every intervening frame between the start and end of a field block.

requirements.quote:
last frame in a sequence of HEADERS or CONTINUATION frames has the
   END_HEADERS flag set.
requirements.condition: For a sequence beginning with HEADERS and continued, if necessary, by CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Set END_HEADERS on the last frame in the sequence.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not end the sequence on a frame without END_HEADERS set.
requirements.why_checkable: The final frame and its END_HEADERS bit are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
END_HEADERS flag set.  The last frame in a sequence of PUSH_PROMISE
   or CONTINUATION frames has the END_HEADERS flag set.
requirements.condition: For a sequence beginning with PUSH_PROMISE and continued, if necessary, by CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Set END_HEADERS on the last frame in the sequence.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not end the sequence on a frame without END_HEADERS set.
requirements.why_checkable: The final frame and its END_HEADERS bit are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
Field block fragments can only be sent as the frame payload of
   HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frames because these frames
   carry data that can modify the compression context maintained by a
   receiver.
requirements.condition: When sending a field block fragment.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the fragment only in the payload of a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not carry a field block fragment in any other frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame decoding can correlate field-block fragment bytes with the enclosing frame type.

requirements.quote:
receiver.  An endpoint receiving HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or
   CONTINUATION frames needs to reassemble field blocks and perform
   decompression even if the frames are to be discarded.  A receiver
   MUST terminate the connection with a connection error (Section 5.4.1)
   of type COMPRESSION_ERROR if it does not decompress a field block.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frames, including frames whose semantic contents will be discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Reassemble and decompress their field blocks even when the frames are to be discarded.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not skip field-block decompression because the containing frames will be discarded.
requirements.error_behavior: If a field block is not decompressed, terminate the connection with a connection error of type COMPRESSION_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send discardable frames that alter compression state and verify both decompression and the mandated connection outcome when decompression is omitted.

requirements.quote:
A decoding error in a field block MUST be treated as a connection
   error (Section 5.4.1) of type COMPRESSION_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When decoding a field block produces an error.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the failure as a connection error of type COMPRESSION_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed compressed field blocks can be injected and the resulting connection-level error code observed.

requirements.quote:
Field compression is stateful.  Each endpoint has an HPACK encoder
   context and an HPACK decoder context that are used for encoding and
   decoding all field blocks on a connection.
requirements.condition: For every HTTP/2 connection at an endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain HPACK encoder and decoder contexts and use them across all field blocks on that connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or decode a connection's field blocks outside its corresponding stateful contexts.
requirements.why_checkable: Sequences using dynamic-table state across multiple field blocks can verify that connection-scoped encoder and decoder state is retained.

requirements.quote:
The dynamic table has a maximum size that is set by an HPACK decoder.
   An endpoint communicates the size chosen by its HPACK decoder context
   using the SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE setting; see Section 6.5.2.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint's HPACK decoder chooses its dynamic-table maximum size.
requirements.required_behavior: Communicate that chosen maximum using SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoder's configured maximum can be compared with the value transmitted in the setting.

requirements.quote:
When a connection is established, the dynamic table size for the
   HPACK decoder and encoder at both endpoints starts at 4,096 bytes,
   the initial value of the SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE setting.
requirements.condition: When a connection is established.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the HPACK encoder and decoder dynamic-table size at each endpoint to 4,096 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not begin the connection with a different dynamic-table size absent an effective setting change.
requirements.why_checkable: Fresh connection state can be inspected or exercised with encodings that depend on the 4,096-byte initial limit.

requirements.quote:
Any change to the maximum value set using SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE
   takes effect when the endpoint acknowledges settings (Section 6.5.3).
requirements.condition: When SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE changes the maximum dynamic-table value.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the changed maximum effective when the endpoint acknowledges the settings.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the changed maximum as effective before the settings acknowledgment.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can compare compression behavior immediately before and after the settings acknowledgment.

requirements.quote:
The HPACK encoder at that endpoint can set the dynamic table to any
   size up to the maximum value set by the decoder.  An HPACK encoder
   declares the size of the dynamic table with a Dynamic Table Size
   Update instruction (Section 6.3 of [COMPRESSION]).
requirements.condition: When an HPACK encoder selects and declares its dynamic-table size.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Dynamic Table Size Update instruction to declare a size no greater than the maximum set by the decoder.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set the dynamic table to a size above the decoder's maximum.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared update value can be decoded from the instruction and compared with the active decoder maximum.

requirements.quote:
Once an endpoint acknowledges a change to SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE
   that reduces the maximum below the current size of the dynamic table,
   its HPACK encoder MUST start the next field block with a Dynamic
   Table Size Update instruction that sets the dynamic table to a size
   that is less than or equal to the reduced maximum; see Section 4.2 of
   [COMPRESSION].
requirements.condition: After an endpoint acknowledges a SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE change that reduces the maximum below its encoder's current dynamic-table size.
requirements.required_behavior: Start the next field block with a Dynamic Table Size Update instruction whose value is less than or equal to the reduced maximum.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another instruction before the required update or declare a value above the reduced maximum.
requirements.why_checkable: The first instruction and its value in the next field block can be decoded and compared with the acknowledged maximum.

requirements.quote:
[COMPRESSION].  An endpoint MUST treat a field block that follows an
   acknowledgment of the reduction to the maximum dynamic table size as
   a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type COMPRESSION_ERROR if it
   does not start with a conformant Dynamic Table Size Update
   instruction.
requirements.condition: When a field block follows acknowledgment of a reduction to the maximum dynamic-table size and does not start with the required conformant Dynamic Table Size Update.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the field block as a connection error of type COMPRESSION_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A nonconforming first field block can be sent after acknowledgment and the connection-level COMPRESSION_ERROR response observed.

requirements.quote:
*  The order in which frames are sent is significant.  Recipients
      process frames in the order they are received.  In particular, the
      order of HEADERS and DATA frames is semantically significant.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives frames on a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Process frames in their received order, preserving in particular the semantic order of HEADERS and DATA frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder frame processing in a way that changes HEADERS or DATA semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: Ordered frame sequences can be supplied and the resulting stream semantics compared with receipt order.

requirements.quote:
*  Streams are identified by an integer.  Stream identifiers are
      assigned to streams by the endpoint initiating the stream.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The initiating endpoint assigns an integer identifier to the stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not have the non-initiating endpoint assign that stream's identifier or use a non-integer identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream creation traces expose both the initiator and the encoded integer stream identifier.
